help: Everything you need, from first launch to a synchronized recording.
The desktop app and browser extension are independent. Choose the section that matches what you installed.
For live desktop audio and uploaded audio/video files.
Windows already includes FFmpeg. Open Advanced settings and save Gemini and Groq keys. Add the 127.0.0.1:10808 proxy only when your connection needs it.
Original audio, dubbed audio, source captions, and translated captions are independent. Any combination is valid.
Only live translation from another desktop program needs a loopback device. The extension and File Studio never need virtual routing.
Drop audio or video into File Studio, select language and voice, then download the two WAV and two SRT outputs or their ZIP.
For live desktop capture: route the source program to AMM Virtual, but keep Avorythm output on your real headphones.
Standalone tab translation—no desktop app, FFmpeg, localhost, or virtual cable.
Open Settings, enter your Gemini key, then check “I allow audio from my selected tab to be sent to Google Gemini.” Start remains disabled until both are ready.
On this page has the lowest practical latency. Synchronized recorder & player starts after a safety lead and is designed for stable dubbing, seeking, and fullscreen.

Use Gemini 3.5 Live for the faster path. Precise mode uses Groq Whisper for complete-utterance timestamps, the free Gemini text pool for translation, and Gemini 3.1 Flash Live for the selected voice; speech and both subtitle tracks share one recorded timeline.

The source tab keeps recording ahead while the player can pause or seek independently. Finish recording whenever you want; a source-video end or YouTube autoplay transition also finalizes it automatically. Refreshing the player restores the active or completed local session.

Fullscreen the Avorythm player for the translated view. Visiting or fullscreening the source tab no longer resets the consumer: capture and synchronized playback keep their independent clocks, while the source remains the producer running ahead.
audioGuide: This is a real Windows setup. Recreate only this route: Chrome outputs to the virtual device, Avorythm captures its virtual microphone, and the dub plays through your physical headphones or speakers.
For Google Chrome, set only Output device to Speakers (AMM Virtual Audio Device). For Avorythm.exe, leave Output device on Default and set Input device to Microphone (AMM Virtual Audio Device).
Play the media in Chrome or the source app so it appears in Volume Mixer.
Open Settings → System → Sound → Volume mixer.
Set the source app output to Speakers (AMM Virtual Audio Device).
Select the AMM loopback/virtual capture inside Avorythm.
Keep Avorythm output on Default or physical headphones and set original volume to zero.
Never route Avorythm output back to AMM Virtual.
That captures the dub again and creates echo or a feedback loop.
For dub-only listening, set Original to 0% and Dubbed to 100%.

The standalone Chrome extension captures its tab directly and needs no virtual device. The in-app audio/video-file processor reads the file with FFmpeg and also needs no Volume Mixer setup. This guide is only for live dubbing of desktop apps or a browser without the extension.

manifest.appDescription: Translate, dub, and caption a selected tab live with Gemini AI, plus an optional synchronized player.

store.short: AI dubbing and live captions for the tab you choose, with an optional synchronized player.
store.introduction: Watch videos, courses, or podcasts in your language. Avorythm uses AI to translate audio from the browser tab you explicitly select, with translated speech and source or translated captions.
store.modes: Choose low-latency playback on the original page or a buffered recorder and player with pause, seek, fullscreen, and customized WebM and SRT export. Original audio, dubbed audio, source captions, and translated captions can be controlled independently.
store.setup: The extension runs independently, without the desktop app, Python, FFmpeg, localhost, or a virtual audio device. Add your own Google AI Studio Gemini key and confirm audio processing in Settings. Optional precise mode also requires a Groq key, host permission, and separate audio consent. Provider free tiers, availability, and quotas can change.
store.privacy: Processing starts only after consent and Start. Selected-tab audio and transcripts go directly to Google Gemini and, in precise mode, Groq for the requested transcription, translation, and voice generation. No advertising, analytics, or maintainer-operated relay server. Keys are session-only by default; remembering each key on this device is optional, not synced, and not encrypted by the extension. Ordinary four-output recording is off by default; synchronized mode records locally for playback and export.
store.limitations: DRM-protected media and internal browser pages may block capture. Live AI processing cannot guarantee zero delay or perfect translations; review important content.
